newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour steps up election sleaze pressure.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour steps up election sleaze pressure.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party on Saturday stepped up pressure on Conservative members of parliament embroiled in sleaze allegations as the campaign for May 1 national elections fell hostage to sex and money scandals.

With Conservative MP Piers Merchant in hiding over Easter after reports of an extramarital affair with a 17-year-old nightclub hostess, attention turned back to former junior minister Neil Hamilton, who is accused of taking thousands of pounds in cash to ask questions in parliament.
Hamilton again denied the allegations, which surfaced more than two years ago, in a letter to The Times newspaper saying he had a right to a fair hearing.

But Jon Kelly, the Labour candidate set to stand against Hamilton in the staunchly Conservative seat of Tatton in central England, said on Saturday he was prepared to step down to make way for a non-political "anti-corruption" candidate.
Kelly said he hoped the move would shame Hamilton himself into quitting.
"Neil Hamilton is a symbol of all that is wrong with John Major's government -- weak leadership, dither, double standards and sleaze," Kelly's campaign manager, Ian McCartney, told a news conference.
The minority Liberal Democrat Party said it was seriously considering joining Labour's initiative and withdrawing its own candidate in Tatton.
The Conservative Party, some 25 percentage points behind Labour in national opinion polls, dismissed the move as an election stunt in a seat which Labour had no hope of winning in the election.

But Liberal Democrat chairman Lord Holme said the proposal had its merits. "I think it's not fair to call it a gimmick but it is certainly a way of dramatising the fact that Neil Hamilton is hanging on in a rather brazen way when many local people, including Conservatives, think he should go," Holme told BBC radio.
Sleaze has dominated the headlines ever since Major set the election date two weeks ago and has thwarted Conservative attempts to capitalise on good economic news.

Another Conservative MP, who admitted taking cash from Harrods department store boss Mohammed Al Fayed to ask questions on his behalf in parliament, resigned earlier this week and a third Conservative MP stepped down after reports linking him to a married woman he is said to have met while attending a clinic for alcoholics.

Piers Merchant, the MP who has been pictured in a tabloid newspaper apparently fondling a mini-skirted blonde teenager, left his home via the backdoor on Friday to escape reporters besieging his family's London home.
He has vehemently denied having an affair with the 17-year-old but has been told by senior Conservatives to clear up the allegations swiftly.
